finding: Case writes could use membership/account state read earlier in the request after that authorization had been withdrawn.
environment: Disposable local Django/SQLite test database with synthetic identities; no real account or investigation changed.

before.observation: All four withdrawn-permission requests increased the case version from 1 to 2; denial was not enforced.
changes_injected: Analyst downgraded to viewer before note save
Analyst downgraded to viewer before disposition
Selected membership removed while foreign-workspace role remains
Database account disabled after initial scope check

correction.behavior: Refresh current account and app role inside the write transaction; acquire permission locks before object locks; bind locked objects to the same authorized app.
correction.data_minimization: Permission query selects required membership keys, role and active flag; account password and profile fields are not selected.

retained_development_failure.cause: A deferred-field query used an unsupported related primary-key alias; 91 test errors exposed it. Corrected by allowing automatic primary-key selection; fresh full verification passed.

limits: Deterministic permission changes at controlled request boundaries; not a timing exploit or evidence of real misuse.
SQLite verification does not prove PostgreSQL row-lock, deadlock or concurrent revocation behavior.
No app-wide security guarantee, independent audit or production validation.
Builder-held hashes identify evidence but do not protect against a trusted filesystem administrator.
